connections.why: Binary representation is what logic gates and Boolean algebra physically operate on
Logic gates are the building blocks of the CPU and its instruction execution
Instructions and addresses are encoded in binary the CPU decodes
Data structures are implemented using a language's primitive types and constructs
Traversal, searching and sorting algorithms operate over these data structures
Algorithms are expressed and implemented through programming constructs
Big-O analysis of these algorithms is part of complexity and computability theory
Abstract data types formalise the structures algorithms manipulate
Applications use programming to query and update databases
Big data extends relational ideas with distributed and functional processing
I/O and addressing concepts underpin how machines communicate over networks
Encoding, compression and encryption are applied to data transmitted on networks
Networked computing raises privacy, security and legal questions
Large-scale data collection drives ethical debates about privacy and surveillance
The NEA project applies object-oriented programming to a substantial problem
The project requires designing and justifying suitable algorithms
Finite state machines and computability frame what algorithms can solve
